name: Infrared Receiver

steps.text: Mount the IR sensor where it will be in the line of sight of the IR remote you plan to use, within 6 feet of an outlet unless you will power IRLinc from an extension cord.
Plug IRLinc into an unswitched wall outlet.
Plug the IR sensor's mini-plug into the jack on the bottom of IRLinc.
If you are using the included credit card remote, remove its battery isolation tab.

If you are using a universal remote, choose a mode on it that you don't use, set that mode to one of the NEC three- or four-digit codes, point the remote at IRLinc from at least 6 inches away and tap its Power button. If the green talk-back LED flashes, the code is compatible; if not, start over with another code.

notes: You can use the pass-through outlet like an ordinary uncontrolled outlet, but don't plug another home automation product into it.
Don't plug IRLinc into a switched outlet or a filtered power strip, and don't stack it with other Insteon devices.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button on IRLinc for 3 seconds, or press and hold the credit card remote's To Scene button for 3 seconds.
Point the universal or credit card remote at IRLinc from 6 inches or more away and tap the button you want it to learn.
For a button that toggles on and off, skip this step. For a discrete on command, tap the SET button on IRLinc; for a discrete off command, double-tap it.
Press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Blue status LED stops blinking and turns on solid

steps.text: Confirm the link by tapping the button you just linked on the remote.

notes: IRLinc Receiver links as a controller; each learned remote button controls the linked responders.
You have 4 minutes to finish before linking mode times out.
The credit card remote's scene control buttons are pre-paired: a device linked to the Up arrow is also controlled by the Down arrow.

steps.text: Set each responder to the state you want the scene to activate.
Press and hold the SET button for 3 seconds to put IRLinc in linking mode.
Tap the SET button to enter multi-linking mode.
One at a time, press and hold each responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
When all responders are linked, tap the SET button to exit multi-linking mode.
Test the scene by tapping the button you just linked.

notes: Multi-linking mode times out after 4 minutes of inactivity.
The Infrared Receiver 2411R Owner's Manual gives these steps for most Insteon controllers in general, not for IRLinc specifically.

verification.note: Generic multi-linking steps from the Infrared Receiver 2411R Owner's Manual; it does not say where the remote button to learn is chosen in this mode.

steps.text: If the responder is a multi-scene device, tap the scene button you want to remove until its LED turns on.
Put IRLinc in unlinking mode: press and hold its SET button for 3 seconds, or press and hold the credit card remote's From Scene button for 3 seconds.
Point the remote at IRLinc from more than 6 inches away and tap the button you want it to unlearn.
Press and hold the responder's SET button for 3 seconds.
steps.expect: Blue status LED stops blinking and turns on solid

steps.text: Tap the button you just unlinked on the remote to confirm.

notes: You have 4 minutes before unlinking mode times out.
Unlink responders you no longer use; otherwise IRLinc retries commands to them and slows the system.

verification.note: The Infrared Receiver 2411R Owner's Manual's unlinking section says to hold the SET button for 3 seconds, the same as for linking, while its X10 section enters unlinking mode by holding the SET button for 3 seconds twice. The catalog uses the unlinking section's single 3-second hold.

steps.text: Unlink any Insteon devices that IRLinc controls.
Unplug IRLinc.
Wait 10 seconds.
While holding down the SET button, plug IRLinc back in, making sure not to let go of the SET button.
Continue to hold down the SET button for 3 seconds.
Release the SET button.
steps.expect: About 20 seconds after release, the blue status LED flashes twice

notes: The blue status LED may or may not be on during the reset.

sources: Insteon Device Categories and Product Keys (October 2008)
